day.readme: Persistent memory compression system built for Claude Code . Claude-Mem seamlessly preserves context across sessions by automatically capturing tool usage observations, generating semantic summaries, and making them available to future sessions. This enables Claude to maintain continuity of knowledge about projects even after sessions end or reconnect. Install claude-mem for Grok Bot: Grok Bot has no host hooks, so we watch the chat log files. Default is CMEM Pro, the hosted memory.

day.description: Computer use CLI for AI agents
day.readme: Computer use for AI agents: read and operate desktop apps through the OS accessibility tree. A CLI and C library for macOS, Windows and Linux. A snapshot returns JSON with a ref for every element an agent can act on. The agent acts on a ref and snapshots again to check, with no pixel matching; the loop stays in your agent. On macOS, CLI calls reuse a private command host for each snapshot namespace and binary build.

day.description: Worktrunk is a CLI for Git worktree management, designed for parallel AI agent workflows
day.readme: Worktrunk is a CLI for git worktree management, designed for running AI agents in parallel. Worktrunk's three core commands make worktrees as easy as branches. Plus, Worktrunk has a bunch of quality-of-life features to simplify working with many parallel changes, including hooks to automate local workflows & copy-on-write build caches. AI agents like Claude Code and Codex can handle longer tasks without supervision, such that it's possible to manage 5-10+ in parallel.

day.description: A hierarchical inference engine for frontier MoE models: hot experts on the GPU (CUDA, Vulkan), warm ones in RAM, cold ones streamed from NVMe. Written in C, runs on the hardware you already own.

day.readme: Tiny engine, immense model. colibri runs very large open models on the machine you already have. A mixture-of-experts model of hundreds of billions of parameters uses only a small part of itself for each token, so colibri keeps that part in RAM and reads the rest, the experts, from the disk when the model asks for them. Pure C, one file per model family, no GPU required. Thirteen engines run today.

Give it any website and it runs a full SEO audit in 10 to 15 minutes, then hands you a clear action plan, sorted by what matters most. It checks everything a good SEO consultant would: Technical SEO. Crawlability, indexing, sitemaps, robots.txt, redirects, page speed and Core Web Vitals. Content quality.

week.description: Vibe code with pi in a lightweight, real IDE that customises itself around the way you work, The Vibe You Need
week.readme: ThinkRail is the agentic IDE that gets better every time you use it, learning your project through living specs today, and building its own capabilities tomorrow. We built a rich interface around the pi coding agent, isolated work into separate workspaces, and gave the agent durable project knowledge through living specs and reusable skills. Skills are folders of instructions, scripts, and resources that Claude loads dynamically to improve performance on specialized tasks. Skills teach Claude how to complete specific tasks in a repeatable way, whether that's creating documents with your company's brand guidelines, analyzing data using your organization's specific workflows, or automating personal tasks.

week.description: A collection of agent skills that help you build great interfaces.
week.readme: A collection of agent skills that cover UI, typography, colors, accessibility, layout, product writing and help you build a great interface. These skills cover topics that I write about on my personal website and my design engineering magazine, Interfaces. better-interface: Reviews a screen, flow or whole interface across accessibility, layout, writing, typography, color and UI polish, and returns one ranked report.

week.readme: A single CLAUDE.md file to improve Claude Code behavior, derived from Andrej Karpathy's observations on LLM coding pitfalls. week.description: 👻 Ghostty is a fast, feature-rich, and cross-platform terminal emulator that uses platform-native UI and GPU acceleration.
week.readme: Fast, native, feature-rich terminal emulator pushing modern features. A native GUI or embeddable library via libghostty . Ghostty is a terminal emulator that differentiates itself by being fast, feature-rich, and native. While there are many excellent terminal emulators available, they all force you to choose between speed, features, or native UIs. Ghostty provides all three.

It orchestrates isolated agents through reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting, candidate validation, structured output, independent record verification, and target-neutral reporting. week.readme: Worktrunk is a CLI for git worktree management, designed for running AI agents in parallel. Worktrunk's three core commands make worktrees as easy as branches. AI agents like Claude Code and Codex can handle longer tasks without supervision, such that it's possible to manage 5-10+ in parallel.

month.readme: Write HTML. Render video. Built for agents. HyperFrames is an open-source framework for turning HTML, CSS, media, and seekable animations into deterministic MP4 videos. month.description: Open source repository of plugins primarily intended for knowledge workers to use in Claude Cowork
month.readme: Plugins that turn Claude into a specialist for your role, team, and company. Built for Claude Cowork, also compatible with Claude Code. Cowork lets you set the goal and Claude delivers finished, professional work. Plugins let you go further: tell Claude how you like work done, which tools and data to pull from, how to handle critical workflows, and what slash commands to expose, so your team gets better and more consistent outcomes.

month.description: Ghidra is a software reverse engineering (SRE) framework
month.readme: Ghidra is a software reverse engineering (SRE) framework created and maintained by the full-featured, high-end software analysis tools that enable users to analyze compiled code on a variety of platforms including Windows, macOS, and Linux. Capabilities include disassembly, assembly, decompilation, graphing, and scripting, along with hundreds of other features. Ghidra supports a wide variety of processor instruction sets and executable formats and can be run in both user-interactive and automated modes.

month.description: Next generation e2e testing framework for web and mobile apps.
month.readme: e2e is an end-to-end testing framework for web and mobile apps. Describe a goal in natural language and an agent drives the app to reach it. Check the result with locators and assertions in the same test. An agent step that a later assertion verifies records its actions, and the next run replays them with no model calls until the app changes. Tests without agent steps need no model.

month.description: Free, local plugin that keeps tool output out of your coding agent's context window. Sandbox and SQLite FTS5 search, 99% fewer bytes in context. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI and 4 more agents. Zero telemetry.
month.readme: The other half of the context problem. Every MCP tool call dumps raw data into your context window. A Playwright snapshot costs 56 KB. Twenty GitHub issues cost 59 KB. And when the agent compacts the conversation to free space, it forgets which files it was editing, what tasks are in progress, and what you last asked for.

new.description: Towards a More Autonomous Agent System

new.description: 手机隐私审计：用 adb 扫出 Android 应用的权限、上报端点与数据流向，并给出可回滚的处置。Desktop Android leak audit: permissions, endpoints, data flows, reversible fixes.
new.readme: NOIR 是一个跑在电脑上的审计工具，通过 adb 读取已连接 Android 设备的应用清单、权限和 APK 里的网络端点，给出分类、风险评分和可执行的处置建议。它也可以在需要时调用 jadx 对单个应用做反编译和关键字检索。 官网 / Website: https://verlintas.dev/noir/ · 中文 盘点：列出所有「有网络权限 + 敏感权限」的应用，以及它们各自拿到了什么。 抽取端点：在设备端用 unzip + strings 从每个 APK 的 dex 里提取 URL，只回传几 KB，不把整包拉回电脑。 数据关联：把权限翻译成"能拿到什么数据"（位置/通讯录/短信/通话/麦克风/相机/屏幕/应用列表/设备标识/文件/日历/账号），再和上报域名配对，得出"哪类数据可能流向哪里"。 共享 UID：识别 android.uid.system 这类共享用户，列出哪些包实际上共享同一套权限并集。 清单层：解析 AndroidManifest.xml 二进制 AXML，找出没有权限保护的导出组件、明文流量、备份、debuggable、targetSdk。...

new.description: Say cheese! Star this repo and your profile picture gets printed out on a receipt printer.
new.readme: Star this repo to have your GitHub profile picture framed, printed out on my receipt printer, and stuck to my wall. GitHub allows you to create webhooks for specific events on your repos, I've set one up for starring this project. When that happens, a payload is POSTed to a Cloudflare tunnel domain, which leads to a PHP script running on a Raspberry Pi that's sitting on my desk. From the inbound request, you can gleen info about the person who starred the repo, like their display name and avatar URL.

new.readme: Make Claude build award-level, cinematic landing pages instead of average AI layouts. AI-built websites tend to look the same for three reasons: a vague plan, no real media, and nobody looking at the result. This skill fixes all three. new.readme: Free, interactive 3D science lessons for high school, physics, chemistry, biology and geography. Try them online: https://lab.tongjiang.app There are 54 lessons so far. new.description: One-click character swap for videos: an open-source, local Higgsfield Genjutsu alternative built on ComfyUI and MiniMax H3, with FLUX.3 Klein relighting.
new.readme: An open-source, Genjutsu-style character and object swap for video. Drop a video and a character photo, press Generate, and the main person in the video is replaced by your character. Or change their hair or clothes, remove something, or put them somewhere else. The camera, cuts, motion and soundtrack stay. Everything runs on open weights on your own GPU: MiniMax H3 for the video, SAM 3.1 to track people, and Qwen3-VL 8B to describe the pictures and shots.

new.description: Pika H3 Flex: video and audio generation inference
new.readme: Built for professional iteration. Pika H3 Flex is a post-trained H3 model, designed to give professional creators the flexibility and speed to explore with precision. Optimized for greater control, it generates video with synchronized audio in six sampling steps and supports up to 12 reference inputs, with shot direction through references and prompts. Pika’s hosted API extends this workflow with 1080p, 2K and 4K video generation, audio stems and prompt enhancement.

new.description: Install Linux next to Windows without a USB stick
new.readme: Install Linux next to Windows without a USB stick. hop is a single Windows app that installs Linux alongside Windows. Pick a system, choose a drive, drag to choose how much space it gets, and click Install. There's no USB stick to find and nothing to install Downloads from official sources. It gets the ISO from the project's own server and verifies its checksum where the project publishes one. You can also use an ISO you already have. Makes room safely.

new.description: Procedurally generated Delft-blue floral page margins for LuaLaTeX, drawn in Lua
new.readme: asked how to make flowers like these in LaTeX. I don't know how the original was made. This project is one possible way, and the way I did it uses hand-authored primitives with randomized parameters, painted in Lua and placed by a procedural layout whose "fill the unused space" part borrows a 1998 idea from the ornament literature. It gets a similar look, but I explicitly tried to not replicate the original.

new.description: Free Claude skill: viral animated story shorts (2D characters in a 3D world) with three.js + Remotion
new.readme: The free Claude skill from the video "How to Make Viral Animated Shorts Using Claude (Full Workflow)". It makes 55-70 s vertical animated story shorts: 2D characters in a colourful 3D world, with ink outlines, a painted town, lens blur, gliding cameras, a march score and sound effects. Everything is rendered with three.js inside Remotion on your own PC, with no AI video generator. Proven on The Bridge That Fell for a Song, a 67 s short about the 1831 Broughton bridge.

new.readme: RuiC-PoseAtlas 是一个完全静态、零依赖的三图鉴参考站，把「人体怎么摆」「衣服怎么穿」「脸长什么样」三件事放在同一个站点里： 姿势图鉴：288 组 AI 生成的去脸人台姿势，每组提供 正面、斜侧、侧面、俯视、仰视 五个视角，共 1,439 张参考图。以「姿态」为单位组织，同一组的五个角度收进一张卡片，打开大图后可以用方向键连续切换，体态、比例、镜头关系一眼可比。 三者合起来的用法很直接：姿势定骨架，衣装定皮相，人像定脸。 先在姿势图鉴里挑一个机位和体态，再去衣装图鉴里找一套同气质的搭配，最后从人像图鉴里选一张脸作为角色参考，三份参考一起丢进生图工具。 很多参考图库的问题是：图片分散、视角不统一、难以把同一姿态的不同角度放在一起比较，服装更是只有一张成品图、说不清到底穿了什么。这个项目以「姿态」「衣装」和「人像」为单位重新组织了三批数据，并为衣装补上了中英日三语标签，让检索这件事真正可用。 同时，它也是一个可以独立部署的前端作品：纯 HTML + CSS + ES Modules，没有框架、没有打包器、没有运行时依赖。克隆下来用一个静态服务器打开即可；需要部署时，直接交给 GitHub...

threats.title: eMudhra intermediate CA private keys compromised
threats.headline: Eight eMudhra intermediate CA keys are recoverable, exposing TLS clients that ship their own CA bundles
threats.summary: The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates were incorrectly generated by the CA, so anyone can recover them from the certificates. Six are TLS intermediates trusted by the Chrome, Mozilla, Microsoft and Apple root programs, and two are codesigning intermediates trusted by Microsoft. An attacker with any of these keys could impersonate any website or service to clients that still trust the intermediates, including apps that ship their own CA bundle and clients that do not enforce Certificate Transparency.

threats.title: vLLM SHM multimodal cache allows forged handles to reach pickle
threats.headline: Authenticated vLLM callers can forge SHM cache handles to run arbitrary Python in worker processes.
threats.summary: When the SHM multimodal processor cache is enabled, vLLM treats an address and monotonic_id pair as authority to read shared memory in the worker. A caller can forge this pair through public HTTP routes so the worker unpickles attacker-staged bytes. This lets an ordinary authenticated inference caller execute arbitrary Python in the worker process, even with insecure serialization disabled.
actions: Check whether your deployments enable the SHM multimodal processor cache.

items.title: Agencies can run security audit sweeps on cheap models after a pass-every-run qualifier
items.connection: The audit skill packages agent-run security review, and the video shows only one of four cheap Chinese flash models fixed security holes in every run.
items.context: small agencies maintain many client repos on thin margins
chain: The cheap flash models are described as tens of times cheaper, which makes audit sweeps across many repos affordable.
The video shows most of them did not pass both tests every run, so a cheap model can quietly miss holes.
Running the audit skill repeatedly on each candidate against seeded flaws gives a simple pass-every-run qualifier before trusting it.
Agencies can offer recurring audit sweeps to every client, priced on cheap-model costs, with the qualifier as evidence.
items.who: Web and app agencies benefit; their clients would pay for a recurring audit line item.
items.versus: Frontier models make sweeps across many small repos too costly, and picking a cheap model blindly risks missed holes.
items.smallest_test: Seed known flaws in three client-like repos and run the audit skill several times on each cheap model. Success: at least one model finds every seeded flaw on every run.
items.disconfirm: No cheap model finds the seeded flaws consistently, or the one that passed the video test fails on the agency's own stack.

items.title: Security audit findings can open ServiceNow tickets owned by the engineer who ran them
items.connection: The Cloudflare audit skill produces machine-readable findings, and AgentCore Gateway now lets an agent call ServiceNow as the calling user with no custom token code.
items.context: enterprise change and risk processes require a named human owner on every ticket
chain: The audit skill gained 8598 stars this week, a sign that agent-run audits with machine-readable findings are becoming standard.
AgentCore Gateway does native on-behalf-of token exchange with Entra ID, so the agent files into ServiceNow as the person who invoked it, not as a shared service account.
Findings land with correct ownership, permissions and audit trail, which is what blocks most enterprise agent rollouts.
Security teams can move agent audits from side experiments into the official remediation queue, and compliance can count them as tracked work.
items.who: AppSec teams in regulated enterprises benefit; CISOs and IT service management owners would pay.
items.variable: time from finding to assigned, tracked remediation ticket
items.versus: Today findings sit in a chat or a JSON file and someone retypes them, or a service account files tickets nobody owns.
items.smallest_test: Wire the audit skill to AgentCore Gateway on one internal repo and file results into a ServiceNow test instance. Success: every ticket shows the invoking engineer as creator and passes the existing ticket permission checks.
items.disconfirm: ServiceNow rejects or reassigns the tickets because OBO tokens lack the scopes the incident or vulnerability tables need.

items.title: Back offices can serve self-checking OCR at scale and route doubtful pages
items.connection: vLLM 0.33.0 adds MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 and Nemotron Parse 3.5, giving production serving to an OCR model that assesses its own correctness.
items.context: insurers, lenders and hospitals still pay people to review scanned documents
chain: MiniCPM-OCR checks whether its own output is correct, so pipelines can route doubtful pages to humans.
Until now it lacked a standard serving path; vLLM 0.33.0 now serves it with new speculative decoding options.
Document teams can run it on the same stack as their text models, with confidence flags feeding a review queue.
Human reviewers see only flagged pages, so review headcount scales with doubt, not with volume.
items.who: Claims, lending and records operations benefit; operations leaders would pay from review staffing budgets.
items.variable: human review minutes per thousand pages
items.versus: Plain OCR forces review of every page or silent acceptance of errors, and hosted document APIs raise data residency issues.
items.smallest_test: Serve MiniCPM-OCR on vLLM 0.33.0 against a labelled sample of real scans. Success: pages flagged as doubtful contain most of the actual errors while being a small share of all pages.
items.disconfirm: The self-check flags pages at random relative to real errors, so routing saves no review time.

items.title: Background coding agents can default to low effort once state tracking is checked first
items.connection: Vals shows low reasoning effort keeps most quality for half the cost, agent-autoloop lets agents run unattended, and StateBench exposes the long-state weakness that unattended runs depend on.
items.context: teams pay per token for agent runs and rarely watch background jobs closely
chain: Vals finds four of seven frontier models keep at least 80% of their index score at the lowest effort for half the cost or less.
agent-autoloop runs CLI agents in the background and only sends a card when a decision is needed, so nobody watches each step.
Unattended work spans many steps of changing state, which is where StateBench shows frontier models fall to 13% or lower on the hardest problems.
Teams can qualify each model at low effort on StateBench-style probes, run the ones that hold up as cheap background workers, and raise effort only on the tasks that fail.
items.who: Engineering managers running coding agents benefit; platform teams paying the inference bill would fund it.
items.variable: inference cost per completed background task
items.versus: Running every background task at high effort wastes spend, while dropping effort blindly risks silent state errors nobody sees until review.
items.smallest_test: Run 20 real backlog tasks through agent-autoloop at low and high effort on one model, after scoring that model on StateBench. Success: low effort completes at least 80% as many tasks accepted at review for half the cost or less.
items.disconfirm: Models that score well on StateBench at low effort still fail long background tasks as often as models that score badly.
